$comment: Agent notes for inline mode, guest queries, prepared messages, Web App query answers and HTML widgets. Shape and rules: scripts/api_notes.py. Every pitfall carries its source label; API means the catalog text quoted in cite.

answerInlineQuery.purpose: Answer an inline query (@bot text typed in any chat) with up to 50 results the user can pick and send.
use_when: the user types @yourbot in a chat and picks something to send
avoid_when: a reply inside the bot's own chat: send a message

pitfalls.text: At most 50 results; next_offset is at most 64 bytes, an empty string means no more pages.
pitfalls.cite: answerInlineQuery: No more than 50 results per query are allowed.; next_offset: Offset length can't exceed 64 bytes.

pitfalls.text: Results are cached 300 s by default and shown to anyone sending the same query; personal results need is_personal.
pitfalls.cite: cache_time: Defaults to 300.; is_personal: By default, results may be returned to any user who sends the same query.

pitfalls.text: Attach an inline keyboard to a result you will edit later; only then does the sent message get an inline_message_id.
pitfalls.cite: ChosenInlineResult.inline_message_id: Available only if there is an inline keyboard attached to the message.

pitfalls.text: Widget content (InputWidgetMessageContent, InputSharedWidgetMessageContent) is refused in production; test server only.
pitfalls.cite: InputWidgetMessageContent: Currently, widgets can't be sent in response to inline queries in the production environment.

pitfalls.text: URLs in results are visible to end users.
pitfalls.cite: InlineQueryResult: All URLs passed in inline query results will be available to end users

answerGuestQuery.purpose: Send the bot's one reply to a guest message: a mention or reply that summoned the bot in a chat it isn't a member of.
avoid_when: chats the bot is a member of: sendMessage
follow-up messages: the bot gets one reply per summons

pitfalls.text: The id is Message.guest_query_id from Update.guest_message; the reply is an InlineQueryResult, not plain text.
pitfalls.cite: Update.guest_message: The bot can use the field Message.guest_query_id and the method answerGuestQuery to send a message in response.

pitfalls.text: Guest queries must be allowed: setMySettings supports_guest_queries.
pitfalls.cite: supports_guest_queries: Pass True to allow guest queries to the bot from chats it isn't a member of

pitfalls.text: That chat may share its id with another bot chat; keep its state separate.
pitfalls.cite: guest_query_id: the message belongs to the chat where the guest bot was summoned, which may not coincide with other existing bot chats sharing the same identifier

pitfalls.text: One reply per summons; no chat history or member list.
pitfalls.cite: https://core.telegram.org/bots/features

pitfalls.text: Whether the reply can later be edited by SentGuestMessage.inline_message_id, and how long the query stays valid, is not stated.

savePreparedInlineMessage.purpose: Store one InlineQueryResult that one user can send from a Mini App through Telegram.WebApp.shareMessage.
use_when: a Share button inside a Mini App that sends a ready message to a chat the user picks
avoid_when: sharing from a chat message: a switch_inline_query_chosen_chat button

pitfalls.text: Only the given user_id can send it.
pitfalls.cite: user_id: Unique identifier of the target user that can use the prepared message

pitfalls.text: PreparedInlineMessage expires (expiration_date); save one right before each share.
pitfalls.cite: PreparedInlineMessage.expiration_date: Expired prepared messages can no longer be used.

pitfalls.text: shareMessage accepts only an id from savePreparedInlineMessage.
pitfalls.cite: https://core.telegram.org/bots/webapps

pitfalls.text: Which chats the dialog offers when no allow_*_chats flag is set is not stated; set the ones you mean.

answerWebAppQuery.purpose: Post a message on the user's behalf to the chat a Mini App was opened from, answering its query_id.
use_when: a Mini App opened from an inline keyboard button, the menu button or the attachment menu posts its result
avoid_when: reply-keyboard Mini Apps: they use sendData
Mini Apps opened from inline mode: their initData is empty

pitfalls.text: web_app_query_id is initData.query_id; verify initData on the server first.
pitfalls.cite: https://core.telegram.org/bots/webapps#validating-data-received-via-the-mini-app

pitfalls.text: With initData.can_send_after, the message can be sent only after that many seconds.
pitfalls.cite: https://core.telegram.org/bots/webapps#webappinitdata

pitfalls.text: inline_message_id comes back only if the result has an inline keyboard; attach one to edit later.
pitfalls.cite: SentWebAppMessage.inline_message_id: Available only if there is an inline keyboard attached to the message.

pitfalls.text: Whether one query_id accepts a second answer is not stated; answer it once.

sendWidget.purpose: Send a message with an HTML widget: fixed code plus public_data and chat_data that only the bot changes.
use_when: a card whose state changes in place (order, score, timer)
is_shared: one live object for many chats
avoid_when: forms, text input or network data: a Mini App
a few choices: an inline keyboard

pitfalls.text: Production: private chats only, and the message is protected content.
pitfalls.cite: sendWidget: Currently, in the production environment, widgets can be sent only to private chats, and sent widgets automatically have protected content

pitfalls.text: Groups, inline results and forwards: test server only.
pitfalls.cite: https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets

pitfalls.text: html is 1-32768 bytes and at most 4096 after zlib level 9 (scripts/validate_widget.py).
pitfalls.cite: html: The code must not exceed 4096 bytes when compressed by zlib with the maximum compression level.

pitfalls.text: HTML can't change after sending; a new layout is a new widget.
pitfalls.cite: https://core.telegram.org/bots/widgets

pitfalls.text: Without allow_queries the widget can't query the bot.
pitfalls.cite: allow_queries: Pass True to allow the widget to send queries to the bot

sendSharedWidget.purpose: Send again, by widget_id, a shared widget the bot created with sendWidget is_shared.
use_when: one live poll or scoreboard shown in many private chats
avoid_when: copyMessage of a widget message: it is refused, re-send by widget_id

pitfalls.text: widget_id is Message.widget.id from the sendWidget call with is_shared.
pitfalls.cite: Widget.id: Unique identifier of the shared widget, which can be used to send the widget again using the method sendSharedWidget

pitfalls.text: public_data is shared by every copy; chat_data is per message.
pitfalls.cite: public_data: If the widget is shared, then all messages with it will have the same public data.

pitfalls.text: Production: private chats only, protected content.
pitfalls.cite: sendSharedWidget: Currently, in the production environment, widgets can be sent only to private chats

answerWidgetQuery.purpose: Answer one query a widget sent (widget_query or shared_widget_query) with up to 1024 bytes for that widget only.
use_when: every widget query, exactly once, also when the action failed
avoid_when: changing what widgets show: editMessageWidgetData or editSharedWidgetData

pitfalls.text: Answer within 15 seconds.
pitfalls.cite: answerWidgetQuery: The query must be answered within 15 seconds.

pitfalls.text: The answer reaches only the asking widget and changes no widget data.
pitfalls.cite: answerWidgetQuery: The answer is received only by the widget that sent the query and doesn't change data of the widget

pitfalls.text: A user can send at most 5 queries per 5 seconds across all the bot's widgets.
pitfalls.cite: WidgetQuery: Each user can send at most 5 queries per 5 seconds to the bot from all its widgets.

pitfalls.text: Query data (1-64 bytes) comes from the widget: check it against the bot's own state.

editMessageWidgetData.purpose: Change public_data and/or chat_data of a widget in a message sent by or via the bot.
use_when: the bot's state behind one widget message changed
avoid_when: a new layout: send a new widget
all copies of a shared widget: editSharedWidgetData

pitfalls.text: Address chat_id + message_id, or inline_message_id for inline messages.
pitfalls.cite: chat_id: Required if inline_message_id is not specified.

pitfalls.text: An omitted field is kept, an empty string clears it; each is at most 1024 bytes.
pitfalls.cite: public_data: pass an empty string to remove the public data. If omitted, then the public data isn't changed.

pitfalls.text: A shared widget's public_data changes at most once per second: coalesce writes.
pitfalls.cite: editMessageWidgetData: Public data of a shared widget can be changed at most once per second.

pitfalls.text: Returns True, not the Message.
pitfalls.cite: editMessageWidgetData: On success, True is returned.

editSharedWidgetData.purpose: Replace the public data of a shared widget the bot created, in every message that shows it.
use_when: a shared poll or scoreboard changed and every copy should show it

pitfalls.text: At most one edit per second per shared widget: coalesce bursts.
pitfalls.cite: editSharedWidgetData: A shared widget can be edited at most once per second.

pitfalls.text: public_data is required and replaces the whole value (0-1024 bytes; empty string removes it).
pitfalls.cite: public_data: New public data of the widget, 0-1024 bytes; pass an empty string to remove the public data

pitfalls.text: cache_time 5-3600 s is how long clients may cache it; omitted keeps the current value (30 by default).
pitfalls.cite: cache_time: If omitted, then the current value is kept, which is 30 by default.

pitfalls.text: Put a revision in the data so a widget can ignore an older cached value.
